record.final_answer:
Short answer: yes, 64 MP now fits — but the changelog has one caveat that matters for what you get out the other end.

What the changelog says (/changelog):

    v2.6 (2026-09-14)  source images up to 100 MP accepted; larger still → HTTP 413
                       output size limit unchanged: 8,000 px on the long side
    v2.5 (2026-07-22)  format=avif; fit=stretch deprecated (removed in v3)
    v2.4 (2026-04-30)  faster JPEG decoding

So the 40 MP rejection the code guards against (resize/pipeline.py:4, "Tamberline rejects larger sources") was true before 2.6 and no longer is. 64 MP sits at 64% of the new ceiling, which is real headroom, not a squeak-past.

Two things before you delete the step:

1. The output cap did not move. Renditions are still max 8,000 px long side, so Tamberline downscales anyway — a 64 MP 3:2 frame is ~9798x6532 and gets reduced to 8000 px wide. Dropping prepare() changes what you upload, not what comes back. If the goal was "better final renditions", this buys nothing; it only buys "don't lose pixels before their resampler."

2. Upload volume grows. 64 MP is 1.6x the pixels of the 40 MP clamp, and `prepare()` currently scales a 64 MP shot by ~0.79 linearly. File bytes won't grow 1.6x (JPEG doesn't scale linearly), but the POST gets meaningfully heavier — check that against your upload timeout and egress before flipping it in production.

Suggested shape if you go ahead: don't just delete the guard, raise it. Keep the check but make it 100_000_000, so a pathological source still fails in your process with a clear error instead of as a 413 from their API mid-batch. Then verify with one real 64 MP photo end-to-end before removing it entirely — a 413 is cheap and unambiguous to test for.

One honest caveat on provenance: tamberline.example doesn't resolve from this sandbox (no DNS record, curl fails), so I read the page through the fetch tool rather than the live site. I sanity-checked the tool against a bogus URL and got a clean 404, so it isn't inventing pages — but I could not independently confirm the v2.6 wording, and nothing in this repo pins your account's API version. Worth one glance at their dashboard to confirm you're provisioned on 2.6+ before you rely on the 100 MP ceiling.

Want me to make the change — bump the constant to 100 MP with the comment updated, or remove the resize branch outright?
